newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY LEAGUE-SUPER LEAGUE TO START BEFORE ARL RIVALS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY LEAGUE-SUPER LEAGUE TO START BEFORE ARL RIVALS.

text.p: Media magnate Rupert Murdoch's
Super League has given itself a two-week head start in the
battle with the existing ruling body for domination of rugby
league in Australia next year.
The 10-team breakaway league will start on February 28 with
a match between Cronulla and Canberra, two weeks before the
rival Australian Rugby League (ARL) kicks off, Super League
chief executive John Ribot said on Wednesday.
Ribot said Super League's competition, backed by Murdoch's
News Ltd, the Australian arm of his media empire, will feature
18 rounds, giving each team nine home and nine away matches.
The inaugural season will end with a tour of Britain by
Australian Super League players, with international matches
scheduled for November 1, 8 and 15.
A world club championship featuring Murdoch-backed teams
from Europe and Australia will be played in two three-week
periods beginning on June 6 and July 18. The finals series
starts in New Zealand on September 26.
Super League's season includes a three-way representative
series featuring one team each from New Zealand and
the Australian states of New South Wales and Queensland,
starting on April 11.
The ARL last month announced Parramatta and North Sydney
would start its 12-team premiership on March 14.
The existing ruling body, established in 1908, last month
lost a long battle for monopoly control of the sport when
Australia's Federal Court overturned a previous ruling banning
Super League until 2000.
